description: Building a health monitoring concept/dashboard for astronauts on long-duration missions, tracking vitals, sleep, and stress with a focus on clear, intuitive design.
summary:
DeepSpace Vitals is an astronaut health-monitoring and mission-support platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It demonstrates how astronaut health information and mission operations can be organised in one accessible platform.

The prototype includes separate Mission Control and Astronaut dashboards, simulated vital-sign telemetry, health indicators, trend visualisations, alerts, crew assignments, mission briefings and communication-status indicators.

The project explores how software could support astronaut health monitoring during future space missions. All displayed health readings are simulated and are not real astronaut medical data.
details:
DeepSpace Vitals was developed to explore how astronauts and Mission Control could monitor health information during space missions.

The platform has two roles:

  • Mission Control (Admin): Mission and crew management, astronaut overview, alerts and briefings.
  • Astronaut: A personal dashboard with mission information, health indicators and updates.

The prototype demonstrates simulated vital-sign readings, health trends and communication statuses such as LIVE, DELAYED and NO LINK.

The project was developed using Base44, Figma, Miro, Canva and ChatGPT.

Important limitation: All health readings and telemetry are simulated. The prototype is not connected to real astronaut medical systems and is not intended for medical diagnosis.
